name: Jira
description: Wakes an agent when a Jira Cloud issue changes status, and lets it read what happened, comment, rewrite the description and move the ticket on. A Team Admin binds their team's Jira site and API token and configures which projects to watch and which status transitions matter (e.g. "In Progress → Ready for Dev"); the broker sidecar holds that credential and polls Jira server-side, so the token never reaches your browser or an agent container. On a matching transition the broker wakes the granted agents and queues the event; the agent drains the queue with the `aee-jira inbox` command-line tool and acts with `aee-jira comment` / `update` / `transition`. This replaces the reverted built-in Jira integration (PR #1539) with an installable, uninstallable plugin — removing it leaves the platform byte-identical. Jira Server / Data Center is not supported; there is no two-way sync.

credentials.description: Jira Cloud site — a bare subdomain ("acme") or a full origin ("https://acme.atlassian.net")
Atlassian account e-mail — the Basic-Auth username for the API token
Jira API token — held only by the broker sidecar, never returned after it is set
Optional: comma-separated custom field names agents may read (e.g. "Team, Sprint"), surfaced by default on show/search/list; leave blank to require an explicit --fields per read
Optional: comma-separated custom field names agents may SET via `aee-jira set-field` (e.g. "Team"); leave blank to forbid every field write. A field not on this list is refused

events.name: status_changed
events.description: A watched issue moved to another status

payload.description: the status the issue moved into

promptLine: When a watched Jira issue changes status you are woken; then work it with `aee-jira`: `aee-jira inbox` (peek the team's queued status changes) / `aee-jira inbox --consume <id>…` (drain exactly the ids from your own wake payload: `id`, or `events[].id` in a digest — never a bare `--consume`), `aee-jira list --project KAN [--status "Ready for Dev"]`, `aee-jira search --jql "<JQL>" [--fields …] [--limit N]` (run any JQL, scoped to your team's bound site & projects — for queries `list` can't express, e.g. a `created` date range, an empty custom field, or a summary match; a `--fields` name that isn't a standard column is read as a custom field and rides alongside the row), `aee-jira show KAN-6 [--fields "Team"]` (also lists attachments, the `parent`/epic key — `show` that key to walk Story→Epic — and `availableTransitions`, the moves reachable from the issue's current status so you can pick a `transition --to` without guessing; `--fields` additionally reads custom fields by their Jira name, e.g. `Team` — an empty field comes back as `null`, so you can tell unset from set), `aee-jira statuses --project KAN` (every workflow status the project supports, grouped by issue type — the full set, independent of any one issue's current state), `aee-jira attachment get KAN-6 <id>` (fetch one attachment's content — text inline, binary saved to a file), `aee-jira attachment add KAN-6 <path> [<path>…]` (upload one or more local files as new attachments — the created id + filename come back per file), `aee-jira comment KAN-6 --body "…"`, `aee-jira transition KAN-6 --to "In Progress"`, `aee-jira update KAN-6 --description "…"` (replaces the whole description — keep what the human wrote and add your section; the previous text stays in Jira's history), `aee-jira set-field KAN-6 --field "Team" --value "<id>"` (set an allow-listed custom field by its Jira name — only fields a Team Admin sanctioned are writable, any other is refused; for an id-bearing field like Team pass the id you read with `show --fields "Team"`; use `--value-json '<json>'` for an exotic field shape; a no-op re-set reports `changed:false`). A transition you make is itself a status change and wakes whichever teammate's trigger names that target status. All Jira access is server-side in the broker; you never see the Jira token.
